surfaces.part: cedar treetop spires and foliage mass

answer.evidence: The object is a skyline of two conical cedar treetops over a dark foliage mass. The silhouette widens from a narrow spire (rows 6-16) to full width 32 at row 19, then stays constant to row 47. The column scans show no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or visible horizontal surface. Instead they show alternating lighter and darker foliage tiers that read as a vertical face. There is no top plane or canopy plane. It is a front-facing elevation of tree silhouettes with a rim-like, irregular top edge.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours against 427 and 567 for the references. Its median is 9 colours per tile against about 108. The cedar spires show roughly 3 green steps (light, mid, dark) with simple stepped tiers, while the references use 5-6 greens in clumped leaf masses with per-clump highlights. Outline pixels are tinted dark green (0% neutral), so there is no sticker outline, and there are no 5x5 flat fills. Texture comes only from the tier edges and a little speckle in the dark backing mass, which is far sparser than the reference leaf clumps and grain. It is a thin, low-colour silhouette that would look flatter and simpler next to the references, so density is much lower even allowing for a small skyline piece.
